[3/3] Alias command/API, Web alias editor and persisted preferences green; 420 tests
[1/3] Add a persistent career alias and remembered Web presentation preferences

impact_assessment.why: The dossier alias was fixed at ZeroCool and the Web theme, audio and CRT controls reset on every reload, so players could not personalize their identity or keep a preferred presentation.
impact_assessment.benefits: A lasting handle improves ownership of the dossier, persisted preferences reduce repeated setup, and reduced-motion support improves accessibility.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: alias mutations touch career.json, while Web preferences stay client-side; dependency: none; concurrency: single-user profile saves; state: old careers must sanitize to ZeroCool and unavailable localStorage must fall back silently.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Normalize the alias on read and write, cap it at 24 characters, save profile atomically, wrap preference storage in try/catch, and cover CLI, API, normalization and default paths with tests.

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Profile alias and preferences complete; project gate 5/5, 420 tests; checklists: passed

[1/4] Add permanent Syndicate and Street standing with contract-pay and shop effects

impact_assessment.why: Contracts and clean runs only affect per-run outcomes and operative trust; there is no lasting faction identity or long-term reward for a playstyle.
impact_assessment.benefits: Standing gives contracts and clean extractions a career-level payoff, makes the Black Market respond to Street reputation, and adds a dossier progression axis.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: career.json gains additive faction_standing and shop prices gain a standing multiplier; dependency: none; concurrency: single-user profile saves; state: old careers default to zero, caps must bound bonuses, and current-run effects should use the standing snapshot taken at run start.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Normalize and cap standings, snapshot them at engine creation, apply bounded multipliers in central payout/shop paths, and cover growth, caps, persistence, old-career defaults and both interfaces with tests.

[1/2] Preserve the run-start faction snapshot across save and load

impact_assessment.why: Standing bonuses are snapshotted at run start, but SaveManager.load rebuilds the engine without the snapshot, so a loaded run loses its contract and shop bonuses.
impact_assessment.benefits: Save/load now preserves the exact run economics, and a later career change cannot retroactively alter a checkpointed run.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: save payload gains an additive faction_standing snapshot; dependency: none; concurrency: atomic save; state: old saves without the field must fall back to the current career standing.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Persist the normalized snapshot, restore it with recomputed bonuses, fall back to career standing for legacy saves, and cover snapshot-versus-later-career behavior with a regression test.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Faction snapshot persistence complete; project gate 5/5, 427 tests; checklists: passed
Task 'task-cyberpulse-faction-snapshot' completed successfully.
[1/3] Add a guarded career reset with automatic backup and save cleanup

impact_assessment.why: There is no in-game way to start a fresh career; permanent progression grows forever, and manually deleting files is unsafe.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can restart cleanly, the old career is preserved as a backup, and stale saves cannot resurrect pre-reset progress.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new destructive CLI/API action; dependency: none; concurrency: single-user profile writes; state: reset must require explicit confirmation, back up the career first, and remove every slot only after the backup succeeds.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Require a literal CONFIRM/RESET token, write an atomic career backup before deletion, clear all slots, rebuild a fresh engine, and cover refusal, backup, deletion and API paths with tests.

[1/3] Add Hard Clear, daily streak and faction standing milestones

impact_assessment.why: The milestone catalog predates difficulty, daily streaks and faction standing, so the new progression systems have no permanent recognition.
impact_assessment.benefits: Hard clears, long daily streaks and faction investment now feed the dossier mastery ladder, giving the newer systems long-term goals.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: catalog grows from 12 to 16 and settlement evaluates four new conditions; dependency: none; concurrency: one-shot settlement; state: old careers simply unlock new milestones on their next settlement and duplicate settlement must stay idempotent.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add the conditions to the existing settlement-time evaluator, keep IDs unique, update catalog-count assertions, and cover each new threshold plus deduplication.
